To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the monotone DNF class is learnable under product distributions; (2) the uniform distribution is the hardest distribution under which the monotone Dnf class can be learned from random examples; and (3) the monotone class is learnable from random examples under the uniform distribution if and only if it is learnable under any constant-bounded product distribution.

monotone DNF formulae of size 2O( n) are learnable from random examples in polynomial time under any constant bounded product distribution, and that various constant-depth monotone circuits on few input variables, such as monotone threshold circuits on n input variables with 3 inputs to each threshold gate and with 3 inputs and 2 outputs to each OR gate, are learnable in polynomial-time under any constant bounded-product distribution.

the class of 2O( √n)-term monotone DNF can be PAC learned under the uniform distribution in polynomial time, and that the classes of monotone constant-depth circuits which have constant output and few input variables are learnable in polynomial-time under the uniform distribution.

the class of all monotone 2 O(√ n)- term DNF formulae is learnable under product distributions, and the class of monotonicity- preserving constant-depth circuits is learnable under uniform distribution.
the class of constant-depth circuits which have a small number of monotone gates on a small number of inputs is efficiently PAC learnable under product distributions.
learning monotone DFN is hard in general, but is possible under the uniform distribution and under product distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, under product distributions, we can efficiently learn any monotone Boolean function that is not a majority of its neighbors.

the class of constant-depth circuits with small fan-in gates and small number of inputs is learnable under product distributions, and the class of constant-width monotone DNF formulae is learnable under the uniform distribution.
monotone DNF can be learned under product distributions, while monotone DNF cannot be PAC-learned from random examples under the uniform distribution, unless E = NP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to the case of nonmonotone functions, monotone functions can be efficiently learned from random examples under product distributions, even if they require exponential-size circuits.
, in the model of learning from independent random examples, monotonicity can be a powerful inductive bias.
the learning problem for monotone DNF formulae is much easier than the general case.
